content.title: Environment Variables and Server-Only Configuration
content.context:
Database URLs, external service keys, and deployment-specific values should not simply be hard-coded into application source.

Next.js supports environment variables.
goals: Master Environment Variables and Server-Only Configuration: Never assume a configuration value is secret just because it came from an environment variable.

content.title: The important distinction
content.text:
Some configuration may be safe to expose to the browser.

Other values must remain server-only.

The dangerous mistake is treating all environment variables as equally secret.

content.question: Where should a private database connection value live?

options.text: In code shipped to the browser

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. In server-side environment configuration
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. In server-side environment configuration

content.title: Public configuration
content.text:
Some configuration may intentionally be available to the browser.

The exact naming and exposure mechanism matters.

The learner's rule should be:

**Never assume a configuration value is secret just because it came from an environment variable.**

content.title: Inspect the boundary
content.text:
Ask:

- Where is this value read?
- Does that code run on the server?
- Could the value become part of the browser bundle or response?
- Should a user ever be able to see it?

options.text: Some configuration can intentionally be public.
Every environment variable is automatically secret from users.
Where the code runs affects what can safely be exposed.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: C. Every environment variable is automatically secret from users.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: C. Every environment variable is automatically secret from users.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: The question is not only “Where do I store this?”
**“Who can see it when the application runs?”**
nextSteps: Classify three imaginary values as server-only or potentially public: a database password, a public analytics ID, and a private signing secret.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
